angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 2,310,420 km at 42.16 pc = 0.73 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 50372: distance 42.158 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.033), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 42.158 +/- 1.391 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 14.4594 +/- 1.0195 mas (same row, RUWE 8.85), 14.2 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 3.321 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 50372: radius 3.321 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 62.191 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.604) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 2,310,420 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 8901 +/- 2820 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 50372: effective temperature 8901 +/- 2820 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.056) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 50372: effective temperature 8901 +/- 2820 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.056) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * lam UMa: spectral type A1IV (1987ApJS...65..581G)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * lam UMa: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * lam UMa: projected rotation speed 50 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2007A&A...463..671R)
rotationPeriodMeasuredSource: Measured in this project from the TESS mission's own 2-minute light curve of sector 21 (packages/telescope-cli/src/archives/tess/reduce.mts), by the method and criteria of Holcomb et al. (2022, ApJ 936, 138): 2.31 d, the light swinging by 0.02% as the star turns

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 570) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 3.9 from 1995A&A...294..536H, the median of its 2 spectra; the 2 published values span log g 3.9 to 3.9, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.0% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1995A%26A...294..536H)
